title: Morning + Evening Rhythm
concept: Two short daily check-ins that keep you actually in touch — the fix for drifting into just running a household together.
whenToUse: When you're drifting, feeling more like roommates, just back from travel, or connection's turned purely logistical.
steps: Morning check-in (5 min or less) — how are you feeling about today? Phones down if you can.
Evening check-in (about 10 min) — how did today actually go, plus one thing you appreciated.
Keep the same times most days.
Note yes or no for each of you for a week; adjust the timing, not how much you're doing.

phrases.text: How are you feeling about today?

working: Phones down through the morning hug (if welcome) and check-in. Ten minutes together in the evening before emails. The drift stays small.
notWorking: “You good?” while scrolling your phone. Going through the motions without actually being present doesn't work.
activity: Pick your exact times for the next 7 days. Keep a visible note you both see. Pair it with your daily check-in.
note: Sun Memory (formerly Kill-Switch): when the system starts to feel like a checklist, set it down. Quick: a few minutes inside one ritual — stop the checklist and return to ease. Full: a declared window of 2–24 hours with no system-talk. Either length pauses system-talk only, never basic communication, safety, childcare or logistics, or a scheduled repair, and either of you can end it by naming a safety concern.
